name: Palomar Observatory
place: Palomar Mountain, San Diego County, California
description: A Caltech observatory in the Palomar Mountains, home of the 200-inch (5.1 m) Hale Telescope. Smaller telescopes there support the Zwicky Transient Facility.
highlights: The Hale Telescope had first light on 26 January 1949, with Edwin Hubble pointing it at NGC 2261.
It was the world's largest optical telescope until the Soviet BTA-6 in the mid-1970s.
Spectra from the Hale Telescope revealed that quasars are extremely distant.
